paragraphs: An experiment comparing several alternatives with a control can include subpopulations that respond differently. This paper evaluates each alternative through a weighted average of its results across those groups. The goal is to identify every alternative that beats the control, while collecting as few observations as possible. The setup assumes homogeneous subpopulations and independent observations conditional on the chosen alternative and group.

The authors propose a sequential strategy that chooses which alternative to test as observations arrive. They analyze three levels of access to group information: group membership is hidden, membership is observed but cannot be selected, or the experimenter can choose the group supplying each response. These settings distinguish information available for interpreting observations from control over how observations are collected.

The strategy achieves the exact optimal asymptotic rate as the required error probability approaches zero: expected stopping time scales with the logarithm of inverse error probability. This is a precise guarantee about increasingly demanding confidence requirements. Numerical simulations using synthetic data and data from an actual experiment illustrate its efficiency.
neurips-2021-a-b-n-testing-with-control-.tldr: A sequential testing strategy identifies alternatives that outperform a control with asymptotically optimal efficiency across three settings for access to subpopulation information.

paragraphs: Transfer learning starts with a model trained on source data and adapts it to a target setting with limited training examples. Earlier empirical work found that adversarial training on the source data can improve this adaptation. This paper investigates the reason for that improvement by examining the representations learned before the target task is introduced.

The authors construct a theoretical model in which adversarial source training produces provably better representations. Within that model, fine-tuning from those representations yields more accurate predictions on target data. The explanation connects transfer performance to what source training teaches the model to represent, providing a mathematical account of the previously observed benefit.

The paper also studies semi-supervised source learning and finds theoretical and empirical evidence that it improves transfer through better representations. Adding adversarial training can improve transferability further, suggesting complementary benefits from the two approaches. Experiments with established datasets and deep learning architectures support the theories. The resulting claim combines guarantees within the theoretical model with empirical support beyond that analysis.
neurips-2021-adversarial-training-helps-.tldr: A theoretical model and supporting experiments explain how adversarial and semi-supervised source training can improve transfer by improving learned representations.

paragraphs: Recurrent neural networks can reproduce animal behavior while arriving at different internal solutions. This creates a problem for neuroscience: matching a task does not establish that a network uses a unique strategy. The paper investigates the structure of these alternative solutions and how they can be compared meaningfully.

The authors begin with a two-neuron network, tracing different final solutions to initial connectivity and identifying distinct dynamical regimes. They then examine delayed discrimination, interval discrimination, and time reproduction. Each task produces a rich collection of solutions. Differences appear in neural activity, while tests of extrapolation expose additional variation that task performance alone can conceal.

To organize this diversity, the authors introduce a compact directed graph that summarizes network dynamics in relation to behavioral inputs and outputs. This representation groups solutions into a handful of types and connects extrapolation behavior to particular dynamical structures and effective algorithms. Neural features partially predict these types. The work offers a way to compare networks through their internal strategies as well as their observed task success.
neurips-2021-charting-and-navigating-the.tldr: Compact descriptions of recurrent network dynamics reveal distinct strategies that can solve the same task yet behave differently when extrapolating.

paragraphs: Many learning problems contain one optimization problem inside another. Stochastic compositional, min-max, and bilevel optimization share this nested structure, but their algorithms and analyses have often been developed separately. Simple stochastic gradient updates remain common in practice, despite a belief that nesting makes their convergence slower than in ordinary optimization.

This paper brings several such update schemes into a unified approach called ALSET, or alternating stochastic gradient descent. Its central contribution is a tighter analysis that uses smoothness properties hidden in the nested problem. Under this analysis, reaching an epsilon-stationary point requires a total number of samples proportional to epsilon to the power of minus two. Stationarity describes the optimization target here; the result does not assert recovery of a global optimum.

Under specified regularity conditions, applications to compositional optimization, min-max problems, and reinforcement learning match or improve the best-known sample complexities. The findings help explain why relatively simple alternating updates can work well without additional algorithmic modifications. They also give several previously separate problem classes a common analytical foundation.
neurips-2021-closing-the-gap-tighter-ana.tldr: A unified analysis shows that simple alternating stochastic gradient updates can reach epsilon-stationarity with O(epsilon^-2) samples under the paper’s conditions.

paragraphs: Collaborative learning becomes difficult when participants have different data distributions, communicate asynchronously, and may behave arbitrarily. This paper studies that combination without designating any participant as trusted. Among n nodes, up to f can be faulty or adversarial, so learning must tolerate misleading contributions as well as legitimate differences between local datasets.

The central result connects collaborative learning to averaging agreement. In this agreement problem, nodes begin with vectors and try to settle near a common vector that also approximates the honest nodes’ average. The authors prove an equivalence, allowing solutions and impossibility results for agreement to inform what collaborative learning can achieve.

Two asynchronous algorithms offer different optimality properties. Minimum-diameter averaging requires n to be at least 6f+1 and attains the best asymptotic averaging constant up to a multiplicative factor. A second method combines reliable broadcast with coordinate-wise trimmed means and achieves optimal Byzantine resilience at n at least 3f+1. Each yields a collaborative learning protocol with the corresponding optimality property. The equivalence also establishes new limits in adversarial, heterogeneous environments.
neurips-2021-collaborative-learning-in-t.tldr: An equivalence between collaborative learning and averaging agreement yields asynchronous protocols with distinct optimality guarantees and new impossibility results.

paragraphs: Deep networks can learn predictive associations that reflect confounding rather than the relationship of interest. This paper addresses spurious correlations caused by observed confounders through a causal training framework. Its focus is on changing the distribution that training seeks to fit, so that the learning objective reflects interventions rather than only observed associations.

Counterfactual Maximum Likelihood Estimation, or CMLE, applies maximum likelihood to an interventional distribution. The authors analyze this idea using a structural causal model. Because observational data generally do not directly reveal that distribution, they derive two upper bounds on the expected negative log-likelihood. These bounds lead to two algorithms, Implicit CMLE and Explicit CMLE, that can train deep models using observational data.

Experiments cover simulated data, natural language inference, and image captioning. Compared with regular maximum likelihood training, the CMLE methods improve out-of-domain generalization and reduce spurious correlations while retaining comparable performance on regular evaluations. The findings support using a causally motivated objective to address observed confounding without giving up ordinary predictive performance in the reported tests.
neurips-2021-counterfactual-maximum-like.tldr: CMLE uses tractable bounds on a causal likelihood objective to reduce spurious correlations from observed confounders and improve out-of-domain generalization.

paragraphs: Video object segmentation requires representations that distinguish regions throughout a video. This paper develops an unsupervised way to learn dense features directly through a fully convolutional model. The formulation makes spatially detailed representation learning part of the training process, connecting the learned features to the dense nature of the segmentation task.

The method samples anchors on a uniform grid and trains the model to distinguish them both within individual videos and across different videos. A straightforward version of this objective produces a degenerate solution. The authors address that failure with a regularization scheme based on equivariance to similarity transformations: segmentation behavior should transform consistently when the input undergoes those transformations.

The resulting objective supports an efficient implementation and fast training convergence. On established video object segmentation benchmarks, the method achieves higher segmentation accuracy than previous work while using substantially less training data and computation. These reported results connect the design choices to both output quality and training efficiency. The regularizer is especially consequential because it makes the otherwise degenerate anchor-based training scheme usable.
neurips-2021-dense-unsupervised-learning.tldr: Dense anchor-based learning with an equivariance regularizer improves unsupervised video segmentation accuracy while reducing training data and computation in reported benchmarks.

paragraphs: Visual recognition benefits from both detailed local patterns and information integrated across an image. This paper argues that visual transformers’ strong global representations leave high-level local patterns insufficiently considered. It introduces DS-Net, a dual-stream network designed to calculate fine-grained and integrated features together and combine them efficiently for image classification.

Each block processes two resolutions through an Intra-scale Propagation module. An Inter-Scale Alignment module allows features at the two scales to exchange information. The architecture therefore includes explicit mechanisms for processing both scales and coordinating their representations. For dense prediction tasks, the authors also introduce DS-FPN, a dual-stream feature pyramid that enhances contextual information.

The reported ImageNet-1k result exceeds DeiT-Small by 2.4% in top-1 accuracy. For object detection and instance segmentation on MSCOCO 2017, DS-Net-Small exceeds ResNet-50 by 6.4% and 5.5% in mAP, respectively. The paper also reports state-of-the-art comparisons against other vision architectures. Results across classification and dense prediction support the proposed architecture’s potential as a shared backbone for multiple visual tasks.
neurips-2021-dual-stream-network-for-vis.tldr: DS-Net combines local and global features through interacting resolution streams, improving reported classification, detection, and instance segmentation results.

paragraphs: Stochastic compositional optimization covers learning problems such as sparse additive models and model-agnostic meta-learning. The paper addresses how to train these problems when data reside on different devices. Existing methods considered by the authors focus on a single machine, leaving a gap between the optimization setting and the distribution of data in larger training systems.

The authors propose decentralized stochastic compositional gradient descent methods. These extend compositional optimization to training across devices and provide a framework for analyzing convergence in that setting. The authors identify their work as, to their knowledge, the first to enable decentralized training for this problem class.

Their convergence analysis shows that the methods can achieve linear speedup with the number of devices. This is a statement about the analyzed convergence rate, linking additional devices to faster optimization. The authors also apply the methods to model-agnostic meta-learning, where experiments support their superior performance. Together, the theoretical and experimental results establish decentralized training as a promising route for scaling the compositional problems studied.
neurips-2021-fast-training-method-for-st.tldr: Decentralized compositional gradient methods enable training across devices with convergence rates that can achieve linear speedup and supporting meta-learning experiments.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks can gain distinguishing power by passing information among groups of vertices, but representing all k-vertex tuples requires O(n^k) memory. Another approach supplies local structural information before learning begins. This retains the O(n) memory requirement of ordinary graph neural networks, while introducing a one-time preprocessing step that can be nonlinear.

The paper develops local graph parameter enabled GNNs as a framework for understanding this second approach. It characterizes exactly which graphs these models can distinguish through a variant of the Weisfeiler-Leman test and through the structural properties they can capture. Their expressive power falls between ordinary GNNs and higher-order alternatives, giving a precise account of the capabilities gained from local information.

The proposed local parameters are cheap to compute and can be added to any GNN architecture. The authors also provide techniques for selecting useful parameters and connect the framework to finite model theory and logic. Experiments across architectures, datasets, and graph tasks show that adding these parameters often improves performance, supporting their practical value alongside the expressiveness analysis.
neurips-2021-graph-neural-networks-with-.tldr: Local structural parameters give GNNs a theoretically characterized increase in expressive power while preserving linear model memory requirements.

paragraphs: Neural sequence models can generate complex outputs quickly, yet those outputs may be inconsistent or incoherent. This paper approaches that problem through the idea of two complementary reasoning systems: one that recognizes patterns and proposes responses, and another that evaluates them logically. The goal is a lightweight way to improve existing sequence models without additional training.

The authors explore several arrangements in which a neural model produces candidate generations and a symbolic reasoning module checks their logical consistency. The symbolic component can accept or reject a candidate. Neural inference mediates between the sequence model and the logical module, providing the connection needed for the two kinds of processing to work together.

Evaluations address robust story generation and grounded instruction-following. The results show that this combination can improve coherence and accuracy in generated outputs. Its practical significance lies in adding a reasoning-based check around an existing generator through a training-free approach. The evidence supports improvements on the evaluated tasks, while the framework describes a broader way to combine learned generation with explicit consistency checks.
neurips-2021-improving-coherence-and-con.tldr: A training-free combination of neural generation and symbolic consistency checks improves coherence and accuracy in story generation and instruction-following tests.

paragraphs: Image classifiers can depend on peripheral attributes that happen to correlate with labels in their training data. Examples that break those correlations can help debias learning, but such examples are often scarce. This paper presents an empirical analysis showing the importance of diverse bias-conflicting examples beyond those already available in a biased dataset.

The proposed method creates that diversity in feature space. It learns separate representations for intrinsic attributes that define a class and peripheral attributes responsible for bias. Crucially, it learns these representations from the plentiful bias-aligned examples. Swapping their latent features produces synthetic combinations that conflict with the usual bias while preserving diverse intrinsic information from the original examples.

Training then uses these diversified features to reduce reliance on the unwanted correlation. On synthetic and real-world datasets, the approach achieves better classification accuracy and debiasing results than the evaluated baselines. The contribution connects an observed scarcity problem to a specific augmentation mechanism: abundant biased examples become material for constructing the kinds of feature combinations that ordinary training rarely encounters.
neurips-2021-learning-debiased-represent.tldr: Separating class-defining and bias-related features enables synthetic bias-conflicting combinations that improve reported classification and debiasing performance.

paragraphs: Inverse problems reconstruct an unknown signal from measurements produced by a known operator and corrupted by noise. This paper studies linear inverse problems in separable Hilbert spaces, assuming zero-mean noise. Its setting includes denoising, deblurring, and X-ray tomography. The authors ask how to learn a generalized Tikhonov regularizer from data instead of specifying it beforehand.

Their first result characterizes the regularizer that minimizes mean squared error. It depends only on the unknown signal’s mean and covariance and is independent of the forward operator. That independence concerns the optimal regularizer itself; the reconstruction problem still involves the known measurement operator. The result identifies which signal statistics determine the preferred regularization within this framework.

The authors then analyze learning from a finite dataset, using either paired signals and measurements or signals alone. They prove generalization bounds under distributional assumptions that include sub-Gaussian variables. Because the bounds hold in infinite-dimensional spaces, progressively finer discretizations do not make this learning problem harder in the sense captured by those bounds. Numerical simulations validate the theoretical results.
neurips-2021-learning-the-optimal-tikhon.tldr: The paper characterizes the mean-square-optimal generalized Tikhonov regularizer and proves learning guarantees that remain valid in infinite-dimensional spaces.

paragraphs: A policy written as a program can expose the procedure an agent follows, making its behavior easier to interpret. Earlier approaches to learning such policies often restricted their form or required demonstrations and other stronger supervision. This paper develops a framework that synthesizes expressive task-solving programs using reward signals alone for the task.

The framework separates learning into two stages. First, it learns a continuous embedding space for programs in an unsupervised manner, with the aim of representing diverse behaviors. It then searches that space for a program that maximizes task return. This structure addresses the difficulty of composing a successful program from scratch by first organizing a space of possible behaviors.

Experiments show reliable synthesis of programs that solve the evaluated tasks. The framework outperforms the tested deep reinforcement learning and program synthesis baselines while producing more interpretable and generalizable policies. The authors also analyze alternatives for learning the embedding and provide evidence for the necessity of their two-stage scheme. The results connect programmatic policy structure with a practical reward-driven search process.
neurips-2021-learning-to-synthesize-prog.tldr: Learning a program embedding before reward-driven search enables interpretable policies that outperform tested reinforcement learning and synthesis baselines.

paragraphs: A protein can be described through its sequence, three-dimensional structure, and surface. This paper introduces HoloProt, a graph construction that connects these descriptions across scales. In this construction, the surface represents coarser detail, while sequence and structural components supply finer information. The aim is to learn representations that combine these complementary views of the same protein.

A graph encoder lets each level incorporate representations from levels below it alongside the graph at its own scale. The learned representation is tested on two different prediction problems: estimating ligand binding affinity and classifying protein function. This evaluates whether the combined information is useful for both a continuous numerical outcome and a categorical biological task.

For binding affinity, the model performs consistently across dataset splits and beats all evaluated baselines on most splits. For function prediction, it approaches the top model’s performance with ten times fewer parameters. The authors also replace the detailed surface with molecular superpixels, improving memory efficiency with little or no performance loss. This offers a more compact version of the multiscale construction.
neurips-2021-multi-scale-representation-.tldr: HoloProt connects protein surface, structure, and sequence in a multiscale graph representation with strong reported predictive performance and compact variants.

paragraphs: This paper studies whether using the exact gradient of an entire training set is enough for efficient generalization in stochastic convex optimization. Its full-batch algorithms access only that aggregate empirical-risk gradient, rather than gradients from individual examples. The category includes gradient descent, mirror descent, and regularized or accelerated variants, so the question concerns a broad class of first-order methods.

The authors prove a separation between these methods and algorithms such as stochastic gradient descent. Stochastic gradient descent can optimize population risk to accuracy epsilon in O(1/epsilon^2) iterations. Full-batch methods face a different requirement: they either need at least Omega(1/epsilon^4) iterations or have a sample complexity that depends on dimension.

The distinction concerns performance on the underlying population, beyond fitting the observed training data. It shows that access to an exact empirical gradient does not eliminate the statistical and computational difficulties captured by this setting. The result is a lower-bound separation for the specified information-access model, with an explicit alternative between more iterations and dimension-dependent data requirements.
neurips-2021-never-go-full-batch-in-stoc.tldr: Full-batch gradient methods face a provable population-risk tradeoff: more iterations than stochastic gradient descent or dimension-dependent sample complexity.

paragraphs: Graph convolutional networks can be vulnerable when an adversary changes the graph structure. This paper examines that vulnerability through matrix perturbation theory, focusing on the symmetric normalized Laplacian commonly used in graph convolution. The central question is which parts of the graph’s spectrum remain comparatively stable under structural changes.

The analysis shows that low-frequency components could be more robust when their eigenvalues lie within a particular robust interval. Low frequency by itself therefore does not establish robustness. This conditional result motivates GCN-LFR, a co-training framework that uses an auxiliary neural network to encourage transfer of robustness from low-frequency components to a GCN-based model.

The framework is designed to attach to different GCN models and improve resistance to structural poisoning attacks. Experiments cover five benchmark datasets and five GCN-based models. They report resistance to adversarial attacks without sacrificing performance when the graph is benign. The contribution combines a more selective theoretical account of spectral robustness with an adaptable training mechanism supported by those empirical evaluations.
neurips-2021-not-all-low-pass-filters-ar.tldr: A conditional analysis of spectral robustness motivates GCN-LFR, which improves resistance to structural attacks across the reported GCN experiments.

paragraphs: When rewards are sparse, a reinforcement learning agent must explore before it has much guidance about useful behavior. Some novelty-based methods can spend a long time in one unfamiliar region while leaving other unfamiliar regions largely untouched. This paper develops NovelD to address that imbalance by assigning approximately equal weight to different novel areas.

The motivation comes from theoretical exploration methods that combine optimistic initialization with visitation-count bonuses and alternate among novel regions. NovelD turns that inspiration into a simple exploration criterion. In MiniGrid analyses, the authors find that it encourages more uniform exploration while emphasizing movement beyond the boundary of what the agent has explored.

NovelD solves all the evaluated static procedurally generated MiniGrid tasks within 120 million environment steps without curriculum learning; the reported previous state of the art solved half. It also achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple NetHack tasks and beats RND in several Atari games. Across the reported tasks, it matches or exceeds several strong exploration methods, providing empirical support for balancing attention across novel regions.
neurips-2021-noveld-a-simple-yet-effecti.tldr: NovelD approximately balances attention across novel regions, improving exploration coverage and performance on multiple sparse-reward benchmarks.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to recover an entire clustering when an oracle can answer questions such as whether two points belong together. The goal is exact recovery with few queries. The authors introduce a general notion of separation, or margin, that encompasses several earlier clustering margins, the support-vector-machine margin, and familiar stability conditions for center-based clusters.

Under their margin assumptions, the authors design algorithms that recover clusters with O(log n) queries in several settings. In m-dimensional Euclidean space, an algorithm handles arbitrary convex clusters in polynomial time and reduces query requirements by a factor of Theta(m^m) compared with the best existing algorithm. The guarantees rely on the stated separation assumptions.

The analysis also covers pseudometric spaces, where clusters need not have a geometric shape, and establishes near-optimal dependence on the space’s packing number. For clusterings described by binary concept classes, the authors characterize when logarithmic-query recovery is possible. For many Euclidean concept classes, that characterization matches their margin condition, connecting geometric separation with the information needed for exact recovery.
neurips-2021-on-margin-based-cluster-rec.tldr: A general cluster-margin framework yields exact recovery with logarithmically many oracle queries under specified separation assumptions.

paragraphs: Multilingual translation models share parameters across languages, allowing languages with little data to benefit from others. Unequal dataset sizes nevertheless create competing optimization pressures. This paper shows that common upsampling of low-resource languages can lead to either underfitting high-resource languages or overfitting low-resource ones, leaving population-level performance poorly optimized.

The proposed Curvature Aware Task Scaling algorithm, CATS, adaptively rescales gradients from different language tasks. Its meta objective steers training toward regions of the loss landscape with low curvature and low loss across all languages. The method therefore uses the geometry of the optimization problem to guide how strongly each task influences shared parameters.

Experiments on TED, WMT, and OPUS-100 cover different degrees of data imbalance. CATS delivers consistent low-resource improvements of 0.8 to 2.2 BLEU without hurting high-resource performance in those evaluations. The authors also report robustness to overparameterization and large-batch training. These findings support adaptive gradient scaling as a promising way to manage imbalance when training large multilingual models.
neurips-2021-robust-optimization-for-mul.tldr: CATS uses loss curvature to adapt language-task gradients, improving low-resource translation without hurting high-resource results in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Combining deep learning with symbolic reasoning can bring together learned perception and structured inference, but principled combinations can be expensive to scale. Scallop addresses this computational obstacle through a system built on probabilistic deductive databases. Its goal is to make differentiable reasoning practical while retaining a controlled relationship to probabilistic inference.

The key mechanism is a provenance framework with a tunable parameter controlling reasoning granularity. This framework generalizes exact probabilistic reasoning, asymptotically reduces computational cost, and provides relative accuracy guarantees. The adjustable granularity gives the system a way to manage the amount of reasoning computation while preserving an explicit accuracy relationship.

On mathematical and logical reasoning tasks, Scallop scales substantially better than DeepProbLog without sacrificing accuracy in the reported comparisons. The authors also introduce a visual question answering benchmark requiring multiple reasoning steps. Scallop outperforms a Neural Module Networks based model by 12.42% and a transformer based model by 21.66%. These evaluations connect the computational framework to both formal reasoning tasks and a visual question answering application.
neurips-2021-scallop-from-probabilistic-.tldr: Scallop makes probabilistic differentiable reasoning more scalable through adjustable reasoning granularity with relative accuracy guarantees.

paragraphs: Neural ordinary differential equations represent deep models through continuous-time dynamics. Their training already requires expensive gradient calculations involving a backward differential equation, making second-order optimization challenging. This paper develops SNOpt, an optimization framework intended to use higher-order derivative information efficiently in that continuous-time setting.

The authors draw on an optimal-control interpretation of neural network training. They show that Differential Programming can derive backward equations for higher-order derivatives while retaining the same O(1) memory cost. A low-rank representation of second-order derivatives, combined with Kronecker-based factorization, then supports efficient preconditioned updates. These ingredients turn the higher-order analysis into an implementable optimizer.

Across image classification, generative flow, and time-series prediction applications, SNOpt converges substantially faster in wall-clock time than the tested first-order baselines. The framework also enables direct optimization of architectural choices such as integration time through second-order feedback policies. The results show how the optimal-control perspective can guide both parameter updates and architecture optimization for the continuous-time models studied.
neurips-2021-second-order-neural-ode-opt.tldr: SNOpt uses optimal-control-derived second-order information to accelerate Neural ODE training while retaining the stated constant-memory derivative computation.

paragraphs: The paper studies quadratic optimization over matrices whose columns are mutually orthogonal and have unit length, a constraint known as the Stiefel manifold. Such problems arise in spectral formulations of graph matching, clustering, and permutation synchronization. Sparse matrices are desirable in these applications, but standard spectral solvers generally do not incorporate sparsity while preserving global optimality guarantees.

The authors modify Orthogonal Iteration, an algorithm for finding a matrix’s dominant eigenspace, to promote sparsity. Their method guarantees a matrix that is globally optimal for the quadratic objective and is also sparse. The scope of that guarantee matters: global optimality is stated for the quadratic objective, alongside the additional sparsity property.

The motivating application is permutation synchronization, viewed as a constrained clustering problem relevant to matching multiple images or three-dimensional shapes. The proposed approach outperforms previous methods in this application. The contribution therefore combines a sparse solution method for an orthogonality-constrained problem with empirical evidence in a setting where coordinating multiple matches is central.
neurips-2021-sparse-quadratic-optimisati.tldr: A sparsity-promoting modification of Orthogonal Iteration preserves global optimality for the quadratic objective and improves reported permutation synchronization results.

paragraphs: Mammalian vision includes parallel pathways with different functional roles. The ventral pathway supports recognition, while the dorsal pathway supports movement-related behavior. Neural network models have mostly focused on the recognition pathway. This paper asks whether a single network trained with a single objective can capture properties of both pathways.

The authors investigate that question using mouse visual cortex data. They train a deep network with two parallel pathways and a self-supervised predictive loss. This combines an architectural feature resembling parallel visual processing with one shared learning objective, allowing the study to examine whether functional specialization can arise within that arrangement.

The trained model fits mouse visual cortex better than the comparison models and captures both dorsal and ventral pathways. These results support the claim that predictive self-supervised learning in a parallel architecture can account for some specialization seen in mammalian vision. The conclusion concerns the functional properties captured by this model and the mouse data studied; it establishes a successful modeling approach for aspects of both pathways.
neurips-2021-the-functional-specializati.tldr: A network with parallel pathways and one self-supervised predictive objective captures aspects of both mouse visual pathways and improves cortical fits.

paragraphs: Categorical features with very many possible values can be difficult to represent efficiently in deep learning. One-hot encodings and entity embeddings may consume substantial space, overfit, or be hard to interpret. Repeated measurements create a particularly relevant case: the category identifies an individual or object observed multiple times under potentially different conditions.

The paper proposes treating these categories as random effects in a regression model. Its LMMNN framework incorporates the corresponding negative log-likelihood from linear mixed models into deep learning. This brings a statistical treatment of category-specific variation into the training objective, giving neural networks a way to account for repeated observations and high-cardinality identity information.

Tests use simulated and real datasets with a single high-cardinality categorical feature, spanning e-commerce, healthcare, and computer vision. They include neural architectures such as convolutional networks and LSTMs. The authors report significant predictive improvements over state-of-the-art alternatives. Multiple categorical features and classification are discussed as possible extensions, so the demonstrated setting centers on regression with one such feature.
neurips-2021-using-random-effects-to-acc.tldr: LMMNN incorporates random-effects likelihoods into neural regression, improving predictions in reported tests with a single high-cardinality categorical feature.
